passages.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
passages.sermon:
A good name is very valuable.
A good name is better than great riches.
Favor is better than silver.
Favor is better than gold.
passages.original: נִבְחָ֣ר שֵׁ֭ם מֵעֹ֣שֶׁר רָ֑ב מִכֶּ֥סֶף וּ֝מִזָּהָ֗ב חֵ֣ן טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
passages.sermon:
The LORD made all people.
Some people are rich.
Some people are poor.
The LORD made both the rich and the poor.
passages.original: עָשִׁ֣יר וָרָ֣שׁ נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ עֹשֵׂ֖ה כֻלָּ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
passages.sermon:
A prudent person sees danger.
He takes cover.
A simple person keeps going.
He suffers the consequences.
passages.original: עָר֤וּם׀ רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה וְיִסָּתֵר וּ֝פְתָיִ֗ים עָבְר֥וּ וְֽנֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
passages.sermon:
Humility means a person does not think too highly of himself.
The fear of the LORD means a person respects and honors God.
God gives rewards to people who are humble and who fear Him.
These rewards are wealth.
These rewards are honor.
These rewards are life.
passages.original: עֵ֣קֶב עֲ֭נָוָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְכָב֣וֹד וְחַיִּֽים׃

passages.text: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.
passages.sermon:
A perverse person walks a dangerous path.
Thorns and snares fill this path.
A person who guards his soul avoids this path.
He stays far from thorns and snares.
passages.original: צִנִּ֣ים פַּ֭חִים בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עִקֵּ֑שׁ שׁוֹמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ יִרְחַ֥ק מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
passages.sermon:
A child needs guidance.
Teach the child the right way to live.
Show the child the correct path early in life.
If you do this, the child will remember it.
When the child grows old, he will not leave this path.
passages.original: חֲנֹ֣ךְ לַ֭נַּעַר עַל־ פִּ֣י דַרְכּ֑וֹ גַּ֥ם כִּֽי־ יַ֝זְקִ֗ין לֹֽא־ יָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
passages.sermon: A rich person rules over poor people.\r\nA borrower becomes a slave to the lender.
passages.original: עָ֭שִׁיר בְּרָשִׁ֣ים יִמְשׁ֑וֹל וְעֶ֥בֶד לֹ֝וֶ֗ה לְאִ֣ישׁ מַלְוֶֽה׃

passages.text: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
passages.sermon:
A person who acts unjustly will face disaster.
He who causes harm will suffer the consequences.
God will destroy the power of his anger.
God will end the strength of his fury.
passages.original: זוֹרֵ֣עַ עַ֭וְלָה יִקְצוֹר אָ֑וֶן וְשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָת֣וֹ יִכְלֶֽה׃

passages.text: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
passages.sermon: A generous man gives freely.\r\nHe shares his bread with the poor.\r\nGod blesses this generous man.
passages.original: טֽוֹב־ עַ֭יִן ה֣וּא יְבֹרָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ נָתַ֖ן מִלַּחְמ֣וֹ לַדָּֽל׃

passages.text: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.
passages.sermon:
A mocker causes trouble.
A mocker stirs up conflict.
Remove the mocker from your group.
Conflict will leave with him.
Quarreling will stop.
Insults will end.
passages.original: גָּ֣רֵֽשׁ לֵ֭ץ וְיֵצֵ֣א מָד֑וֹן וְ֝יִשְׁבֹּ֗ת דִּ֣ין וְקָלֽוֹן׃

passages.text: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.
passages.sermon: A person loves a pure heart.\r\nThis person speaks with gracious lips.\r\nThe king will become this person’s friend.
passages.original: אֹהֵ֥ב טְהוֹר לֵ֑ב חֵ֥ן שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו רֵעֵ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees everything.
The LORD watches over knowledge.
The LORD protects true understanding.
The LORD frustrates the words of the faithless.
The LORD makes the words of traitors fail.
passages.original: עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה נָ֣צְרוּ דָ֑עַת וַ֝יְסַלֵּ֗ף דִּבְרֵ֥י בֹגֵֽד׃

passages.text: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”
passages.sermon:
A slacker avoids work.
He makes excuses.
He says, “There is a lion outside.”
He says, “I will be killed in the streets.”
He uses fear to avoid responsibility.
passages.original: אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל אֲרִ֣י בַח֑וּץ בְּת֥וֹךְ רְ֝חֹב֗וֹת אֵֽרָצֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.
passages.sermon:
An adulteress speaks with her mouth.
Her mouth is like a deep pit.
The LORD becomes angry with some people.
A person under the LORD’s wrath will fall into that pit.
passages.original: שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקָּה פִּ֣י זָר֑וֹת זְע֥וּם יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִפּוֹל שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
passages.sermon: A child often has foolishness in his heart.\r\nDiscipline can remove this foolishness from him.\r\nThe rod of correction drives foolishness away from a child.
passages.original: אִ֭וֶּלֶת קְשׁוּרָ֣ה בְלֶב־ נָ֑עַר שֵׁ֥בֶט מ֝וּסָ֗ר יַרְחִיקֶ֥נָּה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.
passages.sermon: A person may oppress the poor to gain more for himself.\r\nA person may give gifts to the rich.\r\nBoth actions will lead that person to poverty.
passages.original: עֹ֣שֵֽׁק דָּ֭ל לְהַרְבּ֣וֹת ל֑וֹ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר אַךְ־ לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise— apply your mind to my knowledge— for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.
passages.sermon:
Wise people speak important words.
Listen carefully to these words.
Pay close attention with your ear.
Take these words into your heart.
Apply your mind to my knowledge.
Keep my teachings inside you.
This will please you.
Let these words always be on your lips.
passages.original: הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֭שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי׃ כִּֽי־ נָ֭עִים כִּֽי־ תִשְׁמְרֵ֣ם בְּבִטְנֶ֑ךָ יִכֹּ֥נוּ יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו עַל־ שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today—yes, you.
passages.sermon: I want you to trust in the LORD.\r\nI am teaching you today.\r\nI am speaking directly to you.
passages.original: לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם אַף־ אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge, to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you?
passages.sermon:
I have written for you.
I gave you many sayings.
These sayings give you counsel.
These sayings give you knowledge.
I want you to know what is true.
I want you to know what is right.
These words are reliable.
You can use these words to answer others.
You can give true answers to those who ask you.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ שִׁלְשׁוֹם בְּמ֖וֹעֵצֹ֣ת וָדָֽעַת׃ לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ קֹ֭שְׁטְ אִמְרֵ֣י אֱמֶ֑ת לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרִ֥ים אֱ֝מֶ֗ת לְשֹׁלְחֶֽיךָ׃פ

passages.text: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate, for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them.
passages.sermon:
A poor man has little.
Do not rob a poor man.
Do not take from him because he is poor.
Some people are afflicted.
Do not crush the afflicted at the gate.
The LORD defends the poor and afflicted.
The LORD will take up their case.
The LORD will punish those who rob them.
The LORD will plunder those who take from the poor.
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּגְזָל־ דָּ֭ל כִּ֣י דַל־ ה֑וּא וְאַל־ תְּדַכֵּ֖א עָנִ֣י בַשָּֽׁעַר׃ כִּֽי־ יְ֭הוָה יָרִ֣יב רִיבָ֑ם וְקָבַ֖ע אֶת־ קֹבְעֵיהֶ֣ם נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man, or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice about relationships and character.
It warns against choosing certain people as friends.
Do not make friends with a man who is often angry.
Do not spend time with a man who quickly loses his temper.
If you do, you may learn to act like him.
You may copy his ways.
You may trap yourself in trouble because of this.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּ֭תְרַע אֶת־ בַּ֣עַל אָ֑ף וְאֶת־ אִ֥ישׁ חֵ֝מוֹת לֹ֣א תָבֽוֹא׃ פֶּן־ תֶּאֱלַ֥ף אָרְחָתוֹ וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מוֹקֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives a warning about financial responsibility.
It speaks to anyone who considers guaranteeing another person's debt.
Do not promise to pay someone else's debt.
Do not offer yourself as security for another person's loan.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּהִ֥י בְתֹֽקְעֵי־ כָ֑ף בַּ֝עֹרְבִ֗ים מַשָּׁאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
passages.sermon:
If you cannot pay your debt, you have nothing to give.
You owe money, but you cannot repay it.
Why should someone take your bed from under you?
You may lose even your place to sleep.
passages.original: אִם־ אֵֽין־ לְךָ֥ לְשַׁלֵּ֑ם לָ֥מָּה יִקַּ֥ח מִ֝שְׁכָּבְךָ֗ מִתַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone.
Your fathers placed this stone.
Respect the boundary they set.
Do not change what your ancestors established.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
passages.sermon:
A man is skilled in his work.
He does his work well.
He is not lazy.
He is careful and diligent.
People notice his skill.
Kings notice him.
He stands before kings.
He does not stand before unknown people.
He does not serve obscure men.
His skill brings him honor.
His work brings him to important places.
passages.original: חָזִ֡יתָ אִ֤ישׁ׀ מָ֘הִ֤יר בִּמְלַאכְתּ֗וֹ לִֽפְנֵֽי־ מְלָכִ֥ים יִתְיַצָּ֑ב בַּל־ יִ֝תְיַצֵּב לִפְנֵ֥י חֲשֻׁכִּֽים׃פ
